---
title: "Runway vacated"
description: "How OPDI finds the moment an arriving aircraft leaves the runway after landing (runway-vacated)."
---

## In one sentence

`runway-vacated` is the last report of an arriving aircraft on the runway
before it turns off onto a taxiway.

## What it needs

- An arrival **runway pass** (see
  [Take-off and landing times](take-off-landing.qmd#runway-pass-method)).
- At least one report on the runway itself: between the two thresholds and
  within half the runway's width of its centre line.

## How it is computed

1. Take the reports of the arrival pass that lie on the runway itself. The
   reports in the approach area before the threshold are not used.
2. `runway-vacated` is the last of them. It is a received report; its time is
   not interpolated.
3. When the pass holds no report on the runway, no event is given.

## Based on

- Developed for OPDI, on the runway passes of the
  [runway-pass method](take-off-landing.qmd#runway-pass-method).
- The [A-CDM Implementation Manual](../resources.qmd#ref-acdm-manual) has no runway-vacated
  milestone: its taxi-in time runs from landing to in-block. The code `T19`
  in `info.milestone` is a label in the PRU flight diagram, not the manual's number; see
  [Milestones of a flight](index.qmd#milestones-of-a-flight).
- Study: [Flight events from ADS-B, version 4](../../papers/flight-events-v4/index.html).

## What is published

Event type `runway-vacated`, with position, altitude, `distance_flown_nm` and
`time_passed_s`. Its `info` holds `apt_icao`, `runway`, `runway_bearing_deg`,
`traversal_class` (`arrival`), `align_deg`, `max_gs_kt`, `milestone` and
`height_reference` (see the [Data dictionary](../data/dictionary.qmd#info-fields)).

## Use cases

- **Runway occupancy time of arrivals**: `runway-vacated` minus `ALDT`, per
  runway and aircraft type.
- **Use of rapid exit taxiways**: the positions of `runway-vacated` show where
  arrivals leave the runway.

## Limitations

When reception ends on the runway, the event is the last report received,
which can be earlier than the real exit; it can then be at high speed. See
[Limitations: runway events](../limitations.qmd#lim-runway).

## Availability and accuracy

No airport record gives the time a runway was vacated, so accuracy is not
measured. The table gives how often a recorded landing has the event and its
median time after the recorded landing, which is close to a typical runway
occupancy time.
